hero.lede: Lesson Lab started from one question: why does a school's own data — attendance, marks, fees — live in five different spreadsheets instead of one record?

story.title: Software that fits the school, not the other way round.
paragraphs: Most school software sold in this region is built for a different school system first, then translated. Fields get relabelled, but the week underneath still assumes a Monday start and a single calendar.
Lesson Lab is built around a Sunday–Thursday week, Hijri and Gregorian dates shown together, and Arabic as a first-class language throughout — not a toggle bolted on afterward.
It's early. We're working directly with a small number of pilot schools in Saudi Arabia to get the daily details right before opening up further.

values.title: Four things we won't compromise on.

items.title: Arabic-first, not translated
items.description: Arabic and English are both native throughout the system, built together from the first screen.

items.title: Built around the school week
items.description: Sunday–Thursday, Hijri alongside Gregorian — the calendar your school already runs on.

items.title: Your data stays in Saudi Arabia
items.description: Records and backups are kept in-region, with a clear answer on where they live.

items.title: One record, every role
items.description: Admin, teacher, student and parent all work from the same record — not five exports.

cta.title: Talk to the people building it.
cta.description: We're still small enough that you'll talk to the person who wrote the code, not a call center.

hero.lede: Every module below is part of the same record. Mark attendance in the morning and it is already reflected in the afternoon's absence digest — nothing exported, nothing re-entered.

attendance.title: Attendance that matches how the day actually runs.
attendance.description: Teachers mark a section from their own device in under a minute. Admins see today's pattern across the whole school before the first bell has finished ringing.

exams.blurb: Enter marks once — report cards assemble themselves.
exams.title: Marks entered once. Report cards write themselves.
exams.description: Teachers enter marks against the exam structure you set once per term. When the term closes, report cards generate in Arabic and English — no copy-pasting into a template.

Grade scales set once per school, reused every term

fees.blurb: See due, paid and overdue for every student.
fees.title: Know what's owed without opening a spreadsheet.
fees.description: Fee structures by grade and year, dues tracked per student, and a clear due-paid-overdue view for admins and parents alike — in Saudi riyals, recorded as exact amounts.
bullets: Fee structures set per grade, per academic year
Due, paid and overdue visible at a glance
Manual payment recording with a receipt, today

timetable.blurb: Build the week once. Conflicts caught as you build.
timetable.title: Build the week once. Trust it all term.
timetable.description: Set periods, sections and subjects once per term. Lesson Lab stops you from double-booking a teacher or a room before the clash ever reaches a classroom.
bullets: A conflict is caught while you're building it, not after
Every teacher sees only their own week
Changes to one section never move another

messages.blurb: The right message to the right audience, every time.
messages.title: The right message, to the right audience, every time.
messages.description: Send an announcement to a single section, a whole grade, or every parent in the school — and nowhere in between by accident.
bullets: Audience set by grade, section or role
Parents see messages for their own children only
No group chats, no broadcast lists to manage

bilingual.blurb: Arabic and English in the same record, not translated.
bilingual.title: Arabic and English in the same record.
bilingual.description: Every name, every field, every report card carries both languages from day one — not a translation pass bolted on afterward. Hijri dates sit beside Gregorian ones throughout.
bullets: Arabic and English fields, side by side, everywhere
Hijri and Gregorian dates shown together
Right-to-left layout, not a mirrored afterthought

faq.q: Do you charge per student or per school?
faq.a: Per school, based on student count and modules you need — not a per-seat fee that punishes growth.

faq.q: Can we start with one grade before the whole school?
faq.a: Yes. Many schools pilot with a single grade or campus for a term before rolling out further.

faq.q: What happens to our data if we leave?
faq.a: You get a full export of your school's records. Nothing is held hostage in the system.
Yes — WhatsApp and email support both work in Arabic or English, whichever your staff prefer.
